Stronger partnerships with local utilities could better integrate DOW energy needs and resilience into regional generation reserves and interregional transfers, which could enhance access to capacity from less impacted regions during disruptions (Monken et al. 2024). In addition, DOW can adopt a more proactive stance in working with electricity industry partners to expedite and prioritize transmission investments, such as hardening, redundancy, and capacity expansion (Monken et al. 2024). New strategies, including funding mechanisms, might be needed to incorporate DOW energy needs into regulatory and planning processes at the state, regional, and federal levels while aligning DOW energy procurement with broader grid resilience efforts (Monken et al. 2024). Partnerships with local communities can also inform DOW strategies to better maintain functional advanced energy infrastructure, especially in extreme and remote environments, such as Alaska, according to an Arctic researcher. Local expertise on unique risks and possible solutions could inform the testing of advanced technologies and help in the upkeep of remote infrastructure. Technology-specific partnerships with national laboratories and private companies could inform innovation and suitability. 6.10 Common Standards Developing common standards within DOW, the United States, and the international community early in the global adoption timeline could facilitate interoperability and smoother integration of advanced energy technologies into defense operations while also helping to protect supply chains from adversarial influence. For example, adherence to international standards makes the inability of U.S. military aircraft to refuel due to higher SAF concentrations in countries adopting higher blends unlikely, because existing standards ensure compatibility with conventional jet fuel and legacy aircraft. International standards for SAF ASTM D7566 (ASTM 2022b) and aviation fuel ASTM D1655 (ASTM 2022a) ensure that SAF is consistent with the necessary chemical composition and properties for safe use in aircraft engines and fueling equipment (IATA n.d.). Raising awareness of standards can be critical to preparing for operations abroad.
